extracted.intended_audience: eRA Commons users: principal investigators (PIs), signing officials (SOs), program directors/PD/PIs, FSR users, and awardee administrative staff managing submissions and closeout
extracted.subtask_description: Procedures and platform-specific requirements for uploading and submitting additional materials, SBIR/STTR foreign disclosure forms, closeout reports (FFR, Final RPPR, Final Invention Statement, FRAM), and related status tracking in eRA Commons, including role-based permissions and file requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission authority: only signing official (SO) can submit
rubrics_metrics.description: Only signing officials can actually submit the additional materials. Contact principal investigators can add the requested materials and notify the SO via the Submitting Additional Materials to Agency screen, but the SO must sign into eRA Commons and actually submit the materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PI can upload files, enter comments, Save or Delete the draft, and click Notify SO (which sends an email to the SO). The Submit button is visible only to SOs; SOs can view and modify documents before submitting. After submission, a confirmation email is sent and the submission is available to agency staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: UI action labels for Add/Edit Additional Materials
rubrics_metrics.description: In a Status search results list, awardees initially see Add Additional Materials in the Action column (PIs) or under the three-dot ellipsis menu (SOs) for their award. If materials have been added but not yet submitted, the option is labeled Edit Additional Materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NOTE: In the signing official view of Status, the actions Add Additional Materials and Edit Additional Materials appear under the three-dot ellipsis menu for an award.

rubrics_metrics.name: File upload limits and allowed file types for Additional Materials
rubrics_metrics.description: You are limited to 10 files per Additional Materials submission, and the files must be one of these common file types: gif, .jpg, .bmp, .png, .doc, .docx, .xls, .xlsx, .ppt, .pptx, .msg and .pdf; otherwise an error message appears.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can drag-and-drop multiple files simultaneously or click Browse to choose files. For uploaded files you can click View/Download to open or download the file, and click Delete to remove the file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uploaded files are saved immediately
rubrics_metrics.description: Uploaded files are saved immediately with the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Files saved with the request can be previewed, deleted, or edited (prior to final submission). Use Save to preserve the submission and attached materials without submitting so you can return later to add or edit materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments field and visibility to agency
rubrics_metrics.description: In the comments field, enter details on what the material is or why it is being submitted. Any comments entered by the PI and/or SO can be viewed by agency staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PI/SO can also review submissions, including comments, on the Status Information screen. If the agency returns a submission, comments from the agency (rationale) are visible in the Submissions by Awardee area.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission statuses: Submitted and Rejected (returned)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission statuses visible in the Submission by Awardee section include: Submitted — submitted but not yet evaluated by agency; Rejected — submitted and not accepted by agency due to insufficiencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a submission is rejected, the awardee can address rejection comments and make another submission. Returned submissions include a rationale and remain accessible in the Submissions by Awardee area.

rubrics_metrics.name: RADx interim reports via Add Additional Materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain Rapid Acceleration of Diagnostics (RADx) grantees can submit their interim reports using the Add Additional Materials action in the Status module.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow program-specific guide notices (e.g., NOT-OD-21-038, NOT-OD-21-084) and the RADx Programs website for instructions on content and frequency of reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBIR/STTR Foreign Disclosure Form: timing and update frequency
rubrics_metrics.description: After organization receives an SBIR/STTR award, it must submit a form detailing foreign affiliations or relationships to foreign countries at regular intervals and within 30 days of any substantive change. Regular annual updates are required at the time of all SBIR/STTR annual, interim, and final RPPRs; updated disclosure forms are required within 30 days for changes between RPPR submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to all competing applications for funding under NIH, CDC, and FDA SBIR/STTR programs submitted for due dates on or after September 5, 2023. See Required Disclosures of Foreign Affiliations or Relationships to Foreign Countries and relevant guide notices for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBIR/STTR Foreign Disclosure Form: upload and submit behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: While either a PI or an SO can upload the Foreign Disclosure form, write comments, and save the request, only the SO can actually submit the form to the awarding agency. The PDF form must be flattened.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Foreign Disclosure Request link appears on the Status screen (PI in Available Actions column; SO under three-dot ellipsis). Uploaded files are saved immediately. Click Save to save comments; when ready an SO logs in and clicks Submit (PI does not see Submit). A green success message confirms submission and no further changes can be made; the form is immediately available for agency review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closeout: role-based responsibilities (PI, SO, PD/PI, FSR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Closeout tasks differ by funding agency. Program directors/principal investigators (PD/PIs) or signing officials (SOs) can initiate closeout activities, upload files, and save the closeout submission package, but only SOs for the award-holding organization can submit all final reports/documentation. While annual RPPRs can be initiated only by the PI, final RPPRs can also be initiated by an SO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users must possess the appropriate role to act on specific requirements. A user with the FSR role only can go directly to the FFR module and work with FFRs, but cannot access Status or closeout screens unless they also have SO role. Only an SO or a user with delegated report submit authority can submit the reports or other data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Possible Closeout statuses and meanings
rubrics_metrics.description: Closeout Status search dropdown options include: Requires Closeout — grant has not completed the closeout process; Closed — grant has completed the closeout process; In Unilateral Closeout — grant is currently in the process of being unilaterally closed; Unilaterally Closed — grant has been unilaterally closed by the IC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unilateral Closeout is closeout without receipt of acceptable final reports for recipients not in compliance with policy. If Unilaterally Closed, links/actions are not available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closeout Status screen action button lifecycle
rubrics_metrics.description: On the Closeout Status screen, action buttons for a closeout activity start as 'Initiate…', 'Process', or 'Manage…'. After a report is started and saved but not submitted, buttons change to 'Edit…' to review/change the report. After submission buttons change to 'View', and no further changes can be made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some reports allow repeated initiation and resubmission; action button names change accordingly. Role-based visibility means different users will see different actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH/AHRQ Final RPPR: requirement, timing, and differences
rubrics_metrics.description: A Final Research Performance Progress Report (Final RPPR) is required for any grant that has ended and any grant that is not to be extended through award of a new competitive segment; the report is due within 120 days of the project end date. If the recipient organization submitted a renewal application on or before the Final RPPR due date, an Interim RPPR via eRA Commons is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interim and Final RPPR are identical in process and information required; differences: In Interim/Final RPPR only D.1 is required in Participants, Sections F (Changes) and H (Budget) are not part, and Section I (Outcomes) is required. If renewal is awarded after submitting Final RPPR, Final RPPR treated as Interim RPPR; if renewal is not awarded, Interim RPPR will be accepted as Final RPPR. Only PI can initiate RPPR; only SO can submit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final Invention Statement: timing, contents, and submission
rubrics_metrics.description: You must submit a Final Invention Statement (FIS) within 120 days following the termination of a grant award. The statement should include all inventions that were conceived or first reduced to practice during the course of work under the grant or award (from original effective date through completion/termination).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Either a PD/PI or SO can edit the FIS, but only an SO can submit it. Steps: add inventor name, title, date reported; click Add Invention and Save (items saved immediately); use Preview to download a PDF of the filled form. To certify no inventions, click Save with No Inventions then Submit; submission triggers a certification popup and 'Agree and Continue' completes submission. After submission, the PDF is available on the Closeout Status screen.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Financial Report (FFR) requirement and system flow
rubrics_metrics.description: The Federal Financial Report (FFR) is required for closeout and should be prepared according to awarding agency instructions. For DHHS awards, the FFR can be initiated from eRA Commons but users are redirected to the federal Payment Management System (PMS) to fill out and submit the report; for Department of Commerce awards, the FFR can be initiated and completed within eRA Commons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users need appropriate access to PMS; see PMS Help Desk if having trouble. Only a signing official (SO) or a user with delegated report submit authority can submit the FFR; a program director/principal investigator can upload/preview/delete/save the package but cannot submit the final report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final Progress Report Additional Materials (FRAM) and NIH closeout components
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH closeout actions/reports include: Federal Financial Report (FFR); Final Research Performance Progress Report (Final RPPR); Final Invention Statement; Final Progress Report Additional Materials (FRAM) — required only if the agency asks for updates to the submitted progress report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Navigate to topics for each task via the Table of Contents. Actions and requirements may vary by funding agency; check agency-specific instructions for applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing and immutability after submission
rubrics_metrics.description: After you submit additional materials or forms (e.g., Foreign Disclosure Form, Final Invention Statement), you cannot make changes. The form immediately becomes available for agency staff to review and process after submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submission produces a success confirmation (green message). Returned submissions (if rejected) will include an agency rationale and can be resubmitted after addressing insufficiencies.
